transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-29
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Ruiz (Redwood SE), Dr. Lena Ortiz (Head of ML, Vanguardia), Priya Singh (PM), Omar Khan (SRE), Jae Park (CTO)

[00:00] Ethan: hey everyone, thanks for carving time. i'm ethan with redwood, ae on the west coast, with maya our se. quick intros?
[00:08] Dr. Lena: hi i'm lena, lead ML at vanguardia, we run inference for clinical triage models, low latency is important.
[00:14] Priya: priya here, product manager for the platform, focused on cost and observability.
[00:19] Omar: omar, infra, i'll be looking at network and benchmarking.
[00:22] Maya: great, thanks. we'll run through the console, show route-level usage, how to map requests to costs, and where optimize recommendations sit. i'll try to keep to 30 minutes for the demo then leave time for q&a. sound good?
[00:35] Jae: yes sounds good.

Summary/Goals (auto):
- Show per-route dashboards and attribution for model calls (emphasis on clinical routes).
- Demonstrate cost breakdown by model variant, batch settings, and cache hit rates.
- Discuss security (VPC, KMS, audit logs) and how Redwood fits into PHI workflows.

[01:05] Maya: okay i am sharing my screen now, this is the Redwood Consol — excuse me, Redwood Console home. first thing we see is a routes table, you'll notice we group by route id, model, and environment. for vanguardia you'd map your triage endpoints to a route each, eg triage-v1, ocr-extract, followup-scorer.
[01:30] Dr. Lena: is that grouping automatic or we tag it ourselves?
[01:34] Maya: auto-grouping if you send route header, otherwise we fallback to path-based heuristics. you can override with tags. small transcription note: the nav sometimes shows 'Routes' as 'Routs' in older builds, but that's cosmetic.

[02:00] Maya: clicking into triage-v1 route — at the top is throughput/latency sparkline, below is token breakdown and cost per token. the important part is the per-route cost column which decomposes into model compute, batching overhead, and cache savings.
[02:20] Omar: when you say cache savings, is that our prefix cache or kv cache? how is that counted?
[02:26] Maya: good Q. we track both prefix cache and KV cache hits. note, transcript says KV cash sometimes, but it's KV cache — when you have repeated context, hits reduce token compute. the console shows hit rate percentage and estimated cost saved over period.
[02:45] Priya: can we filter by PII-bearing routes? we need to separate PHI traffic for compliance metrics.
[02:50] Maya: yes you can filter by tag or header. many customers create a 'phi:true' tag so dashboards and retention policies apply. retention and hot cache TTLs can be different by route.

[03:15] Ethan: quick pause — enterprise questions we usually get: how is data kept in the control plane? do you write anything to disk? how does KMS work?
[03:23] Dr. Lena: yes, i'd like clarity on KMS and whether any logs include de-identified payloads.
[03:28] Maya: for Private/Dedicated, the control plane metadata is minimal, payloads can stay in customer VPC. We integrate with customer KMS for key rotation, and audit logs are available via our syslog and S3 export. small note: some older docs say 'SOC two' instead of SOC 2, apologies for that.

[04:02] Maya: back to the console — right panel shows cost breakdown by model variant. you can see selection of gpt-large-8q, gpt-medium-16b quant, etc. we rank variants by cost/latency and show percent of requests routed to each.
[04:20] Priya: do you show per-token latency distribution? p95/p99?
[04:24] Maya: yes p50, p95, p99 available and exportable. the p99 is where batching sometimes spikes, so we provide a batching slider in Optimize to simulate throughput/latency tradeoffs.

[04:45] Maya: here's a demo trick — you can open 'Route Insights' which overlays the cost per 1k requests if you change batch size. watch the compute cost drop but observe latency step-ups at certain thresholds.
[05:04] Omar: how accurate is the cost calc vs actual invoice? we need to reconcile for internal chargeback.
[05:09] Maya: we use per-kernel execution time multiplied by our unit rates, there is a small delta vs raw cloud billing due to overheads, but the console exports a CSV you can ingest into billing tools. we'll send a sample export.

[06:00] Dr. Lena: on the model side — we run a few fine-tuned models, and some off-the-shelf open models. can we route to a lower-cost quantized variant automatically on heavy load?
[06:10] Ethan: yes, that's where smart routing + rollout policies help — you can set fallbacks to a quantized variant or shady smaller model for non-critical routes. maya demoed an A/B rollout earlier.
[06:24] Maya: i'll show the rollout panel — you can create a canary where 10% goes to quantized, 90% stays on baseline, and if latency or quality dip thresholds trigger, it will failover to baseline. quality checks can be tied to evaluation prompt sets.

[07:00] Priya: about evaluations — do you keep evals per route so we can detect regressions when we swap model versions?
[07:05] Maya: yes, per-route eval sets and regression alerts; you can attach golden prompts or a small test harness. when model A->B rollout changes quality beyond threshold, console triggers an alert and optional rollback.

[08:00] Maya: now i'll pull up the 'Optimize' suggestions — these are automated recommendations based on observed token distribution, seq lengths, and request concurrency. for triage-v1 we recommend a 32ms KV cache TTL and batching window of 15ms for our observed pattern.
[08:22] Omar: 15ms seems short, we'll need to test in staging. do you provide a simulator?
[08:26] Maya: yes, Optimize has a simulator where you can replay a day's worth of traffic under different batch/cache setups to estimate cost and latency impact. small caveat: the simulator assumes kernel performance from our catalog; local hardware differences matter for Private/on-prem.

[09:05] Priya: can we get route-level RBAC? so only certain teams can change rollout policies?
[09:10] Ethan: yes RBAC and SSO, integrate with SAML/okta. we also persist audit logs for route changes.

[09:35] Dr. Lena: about residency — we are in california, some data must remain in region. can you pin inference to a region or to Dedicated in our cloud project?
[09:43] Maya: yes you can pin routes to region and Dedicated capacity. for strict residency we recommend Private or Dedicated with VPC peering.

[10:10] Maya: demoing a couple more panels — there's a 'Cost heatmap' where green is cache hits and red is high-cost model invocations. you can click a hotspot and see recent example requests (redacted), their model, token count, and latency.
[10:30] Omar: are the example requests redacted automatically? need to be careful about PHI.
[10:34] Maya: yes, by default payloads are redacted in the console; you can request unredacted logs in a secure export if agreed in your contract.

[11:00] Ethan: one question our customers often ask — what does the Dedicated cluster sizing look like for 2k rps of triage at median 120 tokens?
[11:10] Maya: quick back-of-envelope: with a quantized 8-bit variant and batching, you might need a pool of 4 A100-equivalent GPUs with burst to 6. we'll run exact perf tests in a pilot. i've added that as an action item.

[12:00] [demo continues showing CSV export, routing rules, rollout config]

[20:30] Priya: quick - about cost attribution to product teams — can we map routes to cost centers and automatically tag invoices?
[20:36] Maya: yes you can map route tags to cost center codes; we support monthly exports for your finance system and a per-route allocation report.

[22:00] Dr. Lena: any customers in healthcare you can reference for compliance posture?
[22:06] Ethan: we have a few — cannot disclose full names in this recording, but we will share redacted case studies and our compliance pack.

[24:00] Omar: for benchmarking, what's the best way to run a controlled test? we prefer a short window to avoid impacting production.
[24:10] Maya: we suggest a 4-hour window in staging with a static workload replay. we'll provide a harness script and recommend settings to test throughput, latency, and cache hit variance.

[26:00] Priya: question on pricing — is per-token for hosted, and flat for Dedicated? can you explain how to think about unit economics?
[26:12] Ethan: hosted is per-token plus a small request fee; Dedicated is reserved capacity with predictable monthly spend and lower marginal unit cost. the console helps you model both by showing effective cost per 1k requests under your actual traffic mix.

[28:00] Dr. Lena: any limitations around model sizes for Private? we may want to bring larger LLMs to our VPC.
[28:06] Maya: Private supports large models; kernel compatibility is the only caveat. on-prem sometimes needs quantization or specific compilation steps. we'll coordinate with your engineering team.

[30:00] Ethan: okay wrapping up — recap of next steps: ethan to send security docs + sample CSV, maya to prepare Dedicated sizing worksheet and a simulator config, priya to confirm benchmark window.

[30:20] Dr. Lena: sounds good. also can you include sample retention policy configs for phi tagged routes?
[30:25] Ethan: yes will include.

[31:00] Quick Qs and clarifications:
[31:10] Priya: are there per-route alerts for cost anomalies?
[31:14] Maya: yes, threshold-based and anomaly-detection alerts, you can route them to pagerduty/opsgenie.

[32:00] Omar: about network — do you support VPC peering or private link?
[32:05] Maya: both VPC peering and cloud-provider private link options available for Dedicated/Private.

[33:10] Jae: tight question — for the pilot, will the logs show exact tokenization numbers or just aggregated token buckets?
[33:18] Maya: we provide per-request token counts in the export, but in-console we show aggregated histograms unless you export raw events.

[34:00] [short silence, participants typing]

[34:25] Ethan: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the artifacts by end of week. any final words?
[34:33] Dr. Lena: no, thanks, liked the rollout features. excited to test.
[34:38] Priya: thanks, talk soon.

End recap (auto-generated):
- Action items assigned: send SOC2 + security docs, deliver Dedicated sizing worksheet, schedule benchmark window.
- Agreed pilot: dedicated trial + a 4-hour staged benchmark.
- Customer will tag PHI routes and request retention policy templates.

References mentioned: Security pack (link to internal drive - sent on follow-up), Dedicated sizing worksheet (to be created), sample route-level CSV export (to be sent).

[42:00] Meeting ended.
